newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks expected to hold high ground.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks expected to hold high ground.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks are expected to cling onto this week's gains on Thursday, with profit-taking likely to be met by buying at lower levels, brokers said.
"I think the market looks pretty good. Futures were at a high premium yesterday and London (Hong Kong share) prices were up," said Boby Ho, dealing manager at GK Goh Securities.
"I think the turnover is still there," he added.

The Hang Seng index rose 45.62 points to a record close of 13,530.95 on Wednesday. Later the Hang Seng London Reference index gained 46.28 points to 13,577.23. The Hang Seng has risen 414.16 points this week.
Ben Kwong, director of research at Dharmala Securities, said losses on Wall Street overnight might weigh on Hong Kong stocks. The Dow industrials fell 29.07 points to 6,499.34 on Wednesday.

But he said stocks would give ground grudgingly. "Maybe we will see continued buying at low levels so I expect very limited downside. On the upside, continued profit-taking and concern about further fundraising activity by the blue chips will limit the upside in the short-term," Kwong said.
November Hang Seng index futures expire on Thursday. The contract closed at 13,640 points on Wednesday.
